concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a perforated appendix with a collection and surrounding fat stranding on CT.
The patient has a history of prostate cancer in remission and was found to have innumerable hepatic nodules and bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy on CT.
The patient presented with fever, tachycardia, and was found to have pulmonary consolidation on CT.
The patient was found to have a thickened, woody sigmoid colon on exploratory laparotomy and had a history of prostate cancer.
The patient presented with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia, and was found to have a perforated appendix and peritonism.
The patient has a history of heavy cigarette smoking and emphysema.
The patient has a history of hypertension.
The patient was found to have bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy and innumerable hepatic nodules on CT.

rationales.F02: Heavy cigarette smoking increases the risk of lung diseases, including pneumonia and emphysema.
rationales.F05: Prostate cancer in remission could be related to metastatic disease, especially with the presence of innumerable hepatic nodules and lymphadenopathy.
rationales.F06: Acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain is a classic symptom of appendicitis.
rationales.F08: Hypotension is a sign of septic shock, which can be caused by a perforated appendix.
rationales.F10: A perforated appendix with surrounding fat stranding is a strong indicator of appendicitis.
rationales.F11: Innumerable hepatic nodules could be indicative of metastatic disease, particularly in the context of a history of prostate cancer.
rationales.F12: Bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy is suggestive of lymphoma or metastatic cancer, which could be related to the patient's history of prostate cancer.
